audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL specs: alt_bn128 elliptic curve precompiles (EIP-196), EVM control flow instructions (JUMP/JUMPI/STOP), KECCAK256 opcode, difficulty bomb delay (EIP-2384), and no-ether transactions (EIP-7768).

misclassified_entities.reason: From EIP-196: 'Calling Contract' invoking ECADD precompile is internal EVM execution. A contract calling a precompile via CALL opcode is within the EVM execution context, not crossing a trust boundary.
From EIP-196: 'Calling Contract' invoking ECMUL is internal EVM execution, same as ECADD caller. The precompile is called within EVM, not from outside the system.
From EIP-196: 'zkSNARK Verifier Contract' is a smart contract deployed on-chain. It is an internal EVM component, not an external entity. The real external entity is whoever submits the transaction.
From control_flow spec: 'EVM Bytecode' is the contract code being executed within the EVM. It is internal to the execution environment, not an external entity crossing a trust boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-2384: peers broadcast blocks containing difficulty values over unauthenticated P2P. Difficulty must be independently recomputed using the correct formula (with 9M block offset for Muir Glacier). Peers may propagate blocks with incorrect difficulty.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-2384: block producer supplies the difficulty value in the block header. This is received over unauthenticated P2P and must be independently validated against the difficulty calculation formula.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter (Zero-Balance EOA) via Proposer Service
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-7768: zero-balance users submit signed transaction batches to block proposer services. These transactions are untrusted and must have valid signatures, nonces, and proper ordering. The proposer must verify the user's transactions are profitable before funding.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (EIP-7768 Funder) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation with funding transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-7768: block proposer creates Ether funding transactions and includes user transactions in blocks. The proposer is a network participant with no authenticated channel. All produced blocks must be fully validated.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p block import -> Header Validation -> Difficulty Calculation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block difficulty must be independently recomputed using EIP-2384 formula (max(0, block.number - 9,000,000) for fake block number). Peer-supplied difficulty value is never trusted. Timestamp bounds must be validated against parent.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block propagation -> Full Block Validation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All block header fields must be independently validated. Difficulty is recomputed, not trusted from the producer. Block must satisfy all consensus rules for the applicable fork.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Proposer Service -> Transaction Validation -> Block Inclusion
boundary_edges.security_assumption: User-signed transactions must have valid ECDSA signatures and correct nonce ordering. The proposer evaluates profitability before funding. Users cannot steal the proposer's funding Ether because transactions are ordered atomically within the block.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block propagation -> Block Validation -> State Transition
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Blocks containing EIP-7768 funding + user transaction sequences must be fully validated. The funding transaction must precede user transactions in block ordering. All standard block validation rules apply.
